subject.title: Feature: groupScope option to consolidate group sessions into main

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicit opt-in for a selected group chat to share an agent’s private main session, and should that contract include both global and per-binding `groupScope` controls?
rationale: This is a new configuration and session-sharing capability with intentional context-leakage and routing implications; source inspection can establish the missing capability, but cannot choose the acceptable product trust boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow opt-in
options.body: Accept a default-isolated `groupScope` design with explicit trust documentation and review the linked PR as the focused implementation path.

options.title: Design shared sessions first
options.body: Defer this narrow mode until the broader named group/channel/thread session model in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19929 defines the durable abstraction.

options.title: Keep group isolation only
options.body: Decline main-session sharing for groups and retain isolation as the supported boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow opt-in
recommendation.body: Accept a default-isolated `groupScope` design with explicit trust documentation and review the linked PR as the focused implementation path.

likelyOwner.reason: Current routing and session-scope history most strongly connects this person to the affected decision surface.
